# dnsrace 0.8.0 — Adaptive on desktop and Android

dnsrace 0.8.0 is a large release: a new adaptive interface, a real Android build, test
profiles, favourites, recommendation insights, history trends, detailed metrics, and a new
icon. The benchmark engine is unchanged in spirit — it still measures resolvers from your own
connection — but the app around it is new.

This is the first release with an Android APK. Android is a **benchmark and guided-setup**
platform: dnsrace measures resolvers and then walks you through Private DNS or Wi-Fi DNS. It
does not create a VPN, run a background service, use root, or change DNS for you.

## Highlights

### An interface that adapts to the screen

The desktop and phone layouts now share one state model and one set of page components, with
separate shells:

- **Desktop:** a navigation rail, a scrollable content area, a server table with a detail pane,
  and focused dialogs for confirmation and editing.
- **Android:** a top app bar, bottom navigation, 48 dp touch controls, server cards, bottom
  sheets, and safe-area handling for status/navigation bars and display cutouts.
- **Automatic reflow:** the phone layout wraps pills, stacks headers, truncates long resolver
  names, and switches the results grid to full-width touch rows. It fits 360 dp and 320 dp
  screens without horizontal scrolling or clipped tabs.
- **Safe areas:** Android system-bar insets are read over JNI and merged with egui's insets.

The “Signal” visual language replaces the old desktop utility look: deep-ink surfaces, cyan and
mint accents, Inter for UI text and JetBrains Mono for addresses and latency values. All eight
existing themes remain.

### Android 8.0 and newer

- Minimum Android 8.0 (API 26); target and compile SDK 36.
- Universal APK with `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, and `x86_64` native libraries.
- **Android 9+:** the setup guide copies the measured DoT hostname and opens Private DNS.
  Metadata-only hostnames are labelled **“provider's DoT hostname — not measured in this run”**
  and the guide offers a DoT benchmark.
- **Android 8.0–8.1:** the guide shows per-network Wi-Fi DNS steps instead of a Private DNS
  action that does not exist on those versions.
- Detected DNS, network state, and current-DNS labels come from Android's own APIs.
- Reports are shared as text through the Android share sheet. No FileProvider, storage
  permission, or export folder is needed.

The APK contains no Java or Kotlin application code. The whole app is Rust, built with
`cargo-apk`.

### Test profiles

Choose **Quick**, **Balanced**, **Thorough**, or **Custom** on Overview/Benchmark or in
Settings:

| Profile | Timeout | Jobs | Repeat | Cached rounds | Random lookups |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Quick | 700 ms | 24 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Balanced (default) | 1000 ms | 16 | 1 | 3 | 5 |
| Thorough | 1500 ms | 16 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
| Custom | your values | your values | your values | your values | your values |

Editing any advanced value switches the profile to Custom. The profile and test depth are saved
in settings, history entries, and reports. Android defaults to Balanced + DoT; desktop defaults
to Balanced + UDP.

### Favourites

Star resolvers in Servers or in a result card. The **Favourites** filter and **Test favourites**
action appear when at least one resolver is starred; otherwise the action is disabled with an
explanation. Favourites are local only.

### Better recommendations

The recommendation card now explains itself:

- The fastest recommendable resolver, with plain-language reasons (DNSSEC validated, no
  NXDOMAIN hijacking, low jitter, encrypted transport).
- Comparison with your current DNS: faster by milliseconds and percent, slower, or the same.
- A close-call warning when the top two are within `max(2 ms, 10%)`.
- The fastest **plain** resolver that desktop can actually apply.
- The fastest **encrypted** resolver measured in this run. A plain-DNS run does not invent an
  encrypted winner from provider metadata.
- Platform-appropriate actions: **Use this resolver** on desktop, **Set up this resolver** on
  Android. An encrypted selection is never silently swapped for a different provider.

### History trends and detailed metrics

- A sparkline shows the winner's score over the last ten runs (lower is better), with per-point
  tooltips and a “no trend yet” state.
- History entries record the test profile and depth.
- History can be reopened, exported on desktop, shared as a text report on Android, deleted one
  at a time, or cleared after confirmation.
- The detail view shows cached and uncached latency, jitter, timeouts, DNSSEC status, NXDOMAIN
  hijacking status, security classification, endpoint, and provider notes.

### Smaller improvements

- Edit a custom resolver in place; changing its endpoint removes the stale selection.
- About links for the project website, issue tracker, and MIT licence.
- The Android detail sheet can set up a resolver, add or remove a favourite, open the provider
  website, and copy the endpoint.
- The setup guide can switch directly to a DoT or plain-DNS benchmark when the selected result
  cannot supply the value the guide needs.
- The desktop network card can restore the previous DNS.
- The app icon is a deep-ink rounded tile with three ascending cyan-to-mint bars and a mint pulse
  dot, with adaptive, legacy, and monochrome Android layers.

## Fixes

- **The filled favourite star is a proper five-point star.** epaint fills only convex paths, so
  the concave star is now drawn as a centre fan instead of a distorted convex polygon.
- **Copy works on Android 8.0.** The JNI thread prepares a Looper before `ClipboardManager`
  constructs its handler, so the setup guide's copy actions no longer throw
  `Can't create handler inside thread that has not called Looper.prepare()`.
- **The row-detail sheet starts at the top every time.** A fresh scroll identity per opening
  stops the previous sheet's offset from clipping the title.
- **The phone layout no longer breaks after “Test all”.** A long completion notice used to widen
  the scroll page past the screen; notices now wrap, the mobile results grid is a set of 48 dp
  rows, and the app bar keeps 16 dp page padding. Regression tests cover 360 dp and 320 dp with
  long resolver labels and ISP/gateway DNS.
- **Custom resolver actions wrap on narrow phones.** Edit and Remove used to paint over the
  resolver name when the row was too narrow; the actions now flow onto the next line.
- **Back exits cleanly on Android.** Finishing the activity now ends the process, so reopening
  the app always starts a fresh UI instead of a reused zombie window.
- **The About card scrolls itself into view** when opened from the bottom of Settings.
- DNS replies must echo the question (name, type, and class), not just the transaction ID.
- A panicked full-test task no longer freezes progress.
- NetworkManager connection names with escaped colons are parsed correctly.
- Non-UTF-8 platform output is decoded lossily.
- The current-DNS display and `IN USE` badge update after Apply or Revert.
- DoH supports all query types and DNSSEC/AAAA checks.
- Export filenames are collision-safe.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` covers the desktop archives and the Android APK.

### Android install

1. Download `dnsrace-0.8.0-android-release-debugkey.apk`.
2. Allow installs from your browser or file manager when Android asks.
3. Install and open dnsrace. Run a benchmark, then use **Set up this resolver** to follow the
   Private DNS (Android 9+) or Wi-Fi DNS (Android 8.0–8.1) steps.

You can also install over USB:

```sh
adb install -r dnsrace-0.8.0-android-release-debugkey.apk
```

The 0.8.0 APK is **signed with the Android debug keystore**, not a Play Store release key. It is
fine for sideloading and testing. A release-signed APK can be produced later with the same
source and a private keystore.

## Verification

- 255 unit tests and 9 engine integration tests pass on Rust 1.99.1.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo build --release --locked` succeeds for desktop.
- The APK was checked with `aapt2 dump badging` for package
  `io.github.yousef_mohamed22.dnsrace`, version 0.8.0, minSdk 26, targetSdk 36, exactly
  `INTERNET` and `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` permissions, and all three ABIs.
- The phone layout was exercised on a Redmi A7 Pro running Android 16 at 360 dp: every tab,
  every profile, Test all/Test selected/Test favourites, Cancel, the share sheet, all filters,
  favourite toggles, server detail sheets including long titles, history expand/reopen/share/
  delete/clear, Settings save/reset, all eight themes, protocol/family/address-family chips,
  both toggles, steering hostnames, the custom-resolver editor (add, edit, remove, cancel),
  About (including automatic scroll into view), rotation, Back-to-exit and fresh relaunch, and
  a 45-second idle check with no crash or panic.
- Android 8.0 (API 26) was runtime-verified on an x86_64 emulator: install, fresh launch,
  layout at 360 dp, Quick benchmark (26.8 ms), the “Set Wi-Fi DNS” guide with DNS 1/DNS 2
  steps and no Private DNS action, the measured-resolver detail sheet, and Copy without the
  API 26 `Looper.prepare()` failure. The physical Huawei Y7 2018 could not be used because its
  USB data pins never enumerate.
- The installed local APK is `dist/dnsrace-0.8.0-android-release-debugkey.apk` (SHA-256
  `f247258fe8dc2de04bb64dc0ece364c27992c9c455f6ce4e060b758905c57065`). CI rebuilds the
  APK, so the release asset has its own `.sha256`.

The filled-star geometry has a unit test that checks the centre fan covers the star outline
exactly. The Android 8.0–8.1 Wi-Fi DNS branch is also covered by unit tests.

## Limitations

- **No VPN, root, or background service.** Android cannot change Private DNS silently, so
  dnsrace guides you through system settings instead.
- **No iOS or other Apple phone target.**
- **Android reports are shared as text.** The desktop app keeps JSON, CSV, HTML, and summary
  exports.
- **Apply/revert remains desktop-only.** Android is benchmark and guided-setup only.
- **No telemetry or account.** Everything is local.
